description: Zero-drag vacuum parabola launched at 35 deg. Checks apex height (at half-range), return-to-launch-height range, and the two matching times of flight against the closed-form. Exercises the non-trivial two-axis (x and y both time-varying) integration.

source.citation: Closed-form projectile motion, g = 9.80665 m/s^2, no drag. Launch angle t=35 deg, v0=250 m/s. Apex height = (v0 sin t)^2/(2g) at downrange x_apex = v0^2 sin t cos t / g; full range R = v0^2 sin(2t)/g where the projectile returns to launch height; tof to apex = v0 sin t / g, tof to R = 2 v0 sin t / g.

expectations.tolerance_justification: Apex height. RK4/RK45 integrate the quadratic exactly; residual is linear interpolation of the parabola near its flat peak over ~2 m station spacing (~0.1 mm). 2 cm ceiling absorbs step placement.
Horizontal speed constant, so t is exactly linear in x; 1 ms guard.
Return to launch height (drop = 0). Interpolation of the parabola across ~2 m spacing near the crossing is ~0.1 mm. 1 cm ceiling.
t exactly linear in x; 1 ms guard.
